conviction_note: Two things the corpus makes concrete and no summary does: this is the print at which InnovAge sets an initial fiscal-year guide, and its FY26 initial guide was ultimately raised roughly 50% at the EBITDA midpoint - so the bar being set is structurally low - and the company put a confidential draft registration in on 17 July and had an S-3 declared effective on 5 August after a 164% run off the low; both point down, so I take about a quarter of the 11.7% median.

findings.finding: The 8 September print is InnovAge's fiscal-year-end release, at which it issues an initial FY27 guide - and the corpus shows exactly how much sandbagging that guide has historically contained: FY26 was first guided on 2025-09-09 at revenue $900-950m and adjusted EBITDA $56-65m, raised on 2026-02-03 to $925-950m and $70-75m, then raised again on 2026-05-05 to $950-975m and $85-90m, i.e. the EBITDA midpoint travelled from $60.5m to $87.5m (+45%) while the revenue midpoint moved only 4%; the stock has re-rated 164% off its 52-week low on that walk-up and is now being asked to set the FY27 bar from a standing start.

findings.why_not_priced: Each individual guide was wire copy on the day; the sequence is not, and it is what tells you which of this company's four annual prints is the one that disappoints. The baseline's own reaction history reads the same way: the two prints where guidance was raised mid-year produced +37.46% (2026-02-03) and +14.39% (2025-05-06), while the last fiscal-year-end initial-guide print produced -2.81% (2025-09-09) and the quarter after it produced -17.56%. Nothing in the capture - no analyst note, no preview, no consensus - reflects that split; the only sell-side datapoint anywhere in the corpus is a bare 'INNV upgraded' post on 2026-08-21, five days after the Form 3 discussed below.
findings.independence: The tape agrees weakly and independently: the stock has drifted from $11.04 on 08/26 to $10.75 on 09/04 and $10.395 by the 09-08 midday mark on unremarkable 120-250k volume against a 200k average (quote.json), i.e. no accumulation into the print despite the upgrade. none from a different document.

findings.finding: InnovAge submitted a confidential draft registration statement (form DRS) accepted 2026-07-17T19:47:23Z, then publicly filed an S-3 on 2026-07-31 (accepted 20:11:06Z) which was declared effective with the EFFECT notice accepted 2026-08-05T04:15:18Z - five weeks before the print and two weeks after the fiscal year ended - and a Form 3 initial statement of beneficial ownership was accepted 2026-08-17T21:07:23Z with no 8-K item 5.02 anywhere in the lookback to explain a new insider; the company's last 8-K of any kind was item 7.01 accepted 2026-05-18T12:02:06Z.

findings.why_not_priced: Nobody aggregates a DRS, and a confidential draft registration from an already-listed 2021 IPO is not routine housekeeping the way a shelf renewal would be; the pairing of a DRS with a public S-3 two weeks later, effective a month before the print, on a stock that has tripled, is the standard shape of a registered secondary being prepared for the post-print window. If the market had priced a supply event, the run-in would show distribution volume rather than 120-250k-share drift. The Form 3 with no matching item 5.02 is a second unexplained insider-register change in the same four weeks.
findings.independence: Separate source from finding 1 (filings index versus StockTwits digest), and the digest offers no mention of any offering, DRS or S-3 anywhere in its 90 messages - which is itself the point: this reached no one. The one thing that cuts against me is that I cannot read the S-3's body and it may simply be a three-year shelf renewal. none.

baseline_tension: It agrees with the run-in, which is -2.59% over five days and -3.49% over twenty, and cuts against the reaction history's up-bias (3 of 6 up but the two largest moves are +37.5% and +14.4%); the reconciliation I am proposing is that those two were mid-year raise prints and this one is an initial-guide print.
